sub_scenario.family: protected focus blocks versus recurring calendar encroachment
sub_scenario.one_line: CNC machine-shop programmer: yes only if questions batch outside the block

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the fixture program and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The tooling sheet review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Floor questions in the afternoon, while I am verifying finished programs, are welcome.
Verification phase absorbs interruptions.
Absorbs them happily.
Someone new shadowed me in the machine shop this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the program verification into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
Complex fixture programs come out error-free when I write them in sealed morning blocks; the one scrap incident on my record came from a program written between six floor interruptions.
One fragmented program, one scrap bin.
Eleven hundred dollars of scrap, to be exact.
A genuine machine-down emergency justifies breaking any block, and those are rare.
Emergencies are their own category.
A category of maybe four per year.
I archived last cycle's notes on the tooling sheet and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
The shop's quality system now requires my sign-off on all multi-axis fixture programs.
Your precision is a formal control point.
Formal, with my initials on it.
A vendor call about the fixture program ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the machine shop checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the program verification.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the tooling sheet records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Production wants me at the daily nine o'clock floor huddle for live tooling questions, which would cut the fixture-programming block in half every day.
A standing daily cut into the block.
Half the block, every day, for questions that mostly can wait.
I sketched next week's plan for the program verification before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the fixture program updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Most huddle questions, by my own tally, are answerable at eleven-thirty with zero production impact.
The tally undermines the urgency claim.
The tally is why I have conditions instead of a refusal.
The production manager says programmers who skip huddles lose the floor's trust.
Trust framed as attendance.
Attendance is the cheapest proxy they had.
I closed the week by updating the machine shop handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Production wants my answer on the standing nine o'clock huddle seat. What terms do I set before accepting?
